id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_invitations.id. UUID format.

email.description: Email address of the invited person.
email.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_invitations.email. Email format validation enforced.

status.description: Current status of the invitation.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_invitations.status. Values: 'pending' (awaiting user registration), 'accepted' (user joined organization), 'cancelled' (revoked by administrator).

role.description: The role that will be or was assigned to the invited person upon acceptance.
role.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via erp_hrm_invitations.role_id to erp_hrm_roles.id. Returns IErpHrmRole.ISummary containing id, name, isBuiltin, createdAt. FK column role_id is excluded from DTO in favor of this relation object.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the invitation was created.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_invitations.created_at. ISO 8601 timestamp format.

IErpHrmInvitation.ISummary.description: Lightweight invitation summary for organization invitation list displays. Contains essential information for managing the invitation lifecycle: the invited email address, assigned role with name, and current invitation status.
IErpHrmInvitation.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Lightweight invitation summary for list displays within organization context. Direct column mappings: id, email, status, created_at from erp_hrm_invitations table. The role property is populated via JOIN with erp_hrm_roles through the role_id foreign key, returning IErpHrmRole.ISummary. Excluded: organization_id (inferred from endpoint path context), role_id (replaced by role object), updated_at and deleted_at (not needed for summary display), organization relation (context already established).

departmentId.description: Department assignment for the employee. Provide a valid department UUID to assign the employee to a department, or null to remove their current department affiliation. The department must exist within the current organization.
departmentId.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_employees.erp_hrm_department_id FK column. Nullable - set to UUID to assign employee to a department, set to null to unassign (remove department affiliation). Validation: if not null, verify the department exists in current organization context (erp_hrm_departments.id with matching organization_id).

position.description: Job title or position within the organization. Examples include 'Software Engineer', 'Marketing Manager', 'HR Specialist', etc. This is distinct from the system role and reflects the employee's official designation.
position.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping to erp_hrm_employees.position column. Nullable string field for job title or position designation (e.g., 'Software Engineer', 'Marketing Manager'). No validation constraints beyond being a valid string.

employmentType.description: Employment classification within the organization. Valid values: 'full_time' for standard full-time employees working regular hours, 'part_time' for employees working reduced hours, 'contractor' for external workers engaged on a contract basis, or 'intern' for temporary training positions.
employmentType.x-autobe-specification: Maps to erp_hrm_employees.employment_type column. Enum validation required: must be one of 'full_time' (standard full-time hours), 'part_time' (reduced hours), 'contractor' (external workers on contract basis), or 'intern' (temporary training positions).

IErpHrmEmployee.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating an employee's organizational information within the current organization. Allows modification of department affiliation, job position title, and employment classification. All fields are optional to support partial updates.
IErpHrmEmployee.IUpdate.x-autobe-specification: Update employee record with provided fields. All fields are optional for partial update support. departmentId: FK to erp_hrm_departments.id via erp_hrm_department_id column, set to null to unassign department. position: string for job title via position column, nullable. employmentType: enum (full_time, part_time, contractor, intern) via employment_type column. Validate employmentType is one of allowed values. Validate departmentId exists in current organization if provided (not null). Excluded: erp_hrm_role_id (use role change API), status (use activate/deactivate APIs), erp_hrm_member_id/erp_hrm_organization_id (immutable identity), id/created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (system-managed).

displayName.description: Human-readable name that identifies the member to others within organizations.
displayName.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_members.display_name. Stored directly as provided.

IErpHrmMember.IJoin.description: Request body for creating a new member account with email and password credentials, establishing the member's identity in the platform. This creates the base user account; organization membership is handled separately through invitation acceptance. The member can then authenticate using the credentials provided here and join organizations they are invited to.
IErpHrmMember.IJoin.x-autobe-specification: INSERT into erp_hrm_members table. Email must be unique across platform (validate before insert, reject if duplicate). Password is plaintext input to be hashed with bcrypt/argon2 before storage in password column. DisplayName stored directly. PhoneNumber and avatarImage are optional nullable fields. Session context (href, referrer, ip) recorded for security audit trail. All fields map directly to erp_hrm_members columns except password which is hashed before storage.

id.description: Unique identifier for the project.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.id. UUID primary key auto-generated on creation.

name.description: Project name for identification and display.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.name. Required string for project identification.

description.description: Detailed description of the project's purpose and scope. Null if not provided.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.description. Nullable text field for additional project context.

colorCode.description: Hex color code for UI display (e.g., #FF5733).
colorCode.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.color_code. Required hex color string (e.g., #FF5733) for UI display.

status.description: Project lifecycle status: 'active' (can receive timelogs), 'archived' (preserved but inactive), or 'completed' (work finished).
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.status. Enum values: 'active' (accepts timelogs), 'archived' (inactive), 'completed' (finished). Defaults to 'active' on creation.

budgetHours.description: Total estimated hours for budget tracking. Null if no budget set.
budgetHours.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.budget_hours. Nullable decimal for estimated total effort hours.

startDate.description: Optional project start date for scheduling.
startDate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.start_date. Nullable timestamp for project scheduling.

endDate.description: Optional project end date for scheduling.
endDate.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.end_date. Nullable timestamp for project scheduling. Must be >= start_date when both provided.

organization.x-autobe-specification: JOIN via organization_id to erp_hrm_organizations. Returns IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary with org details.

tasks.x-autobe-specification: JOIN on project_id to erp_hrm_tasks where deleted_at IS NULL. Returns IErpHrmTask.ISummary[] for active tasks. Has-many relation with custom filtering logic.

timelogsCount.description: Number of timelogs recorded for this project.
timelogsCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) from erp_hrm_timelogs where project_id matches this project's id.

membersCount.description: Number of employees assigned to this project.
membersCount.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) from erp_hrm_project_members where project_id matches this project's id.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the project was created.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.created_at. Auto-set timestamp on creation.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the project was last updated.
updatedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.updated_at. Auto-updated timestamp on modification.

deletedAt.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active projects.
deletedAt.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from erp_hrm_projects.deleted_at. Nullable timestamp set on soft deletion.

IErpHrmProject.description: Complete project entity representing a work container within an organization. Projects group tasks and track time, with optional budget hours for utilization tracking. Includes project metadata, lifecycle status, assigned tasks, and member count for dashboard displays.
IErpHrmProject.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping: id, name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at from erp_hrm_projects table. Relation: organization fetched via organization_id JOIN to erp_hrm_organizations, returned as IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary. HAS-MANY: tasks fetched via JOIN on project_id to erp_hrm_tasks (deleted_at IS NULL), returned as IErpHrmTask.ISummary[]. Aggregation: timelogsCount = COUNT(*) from erp_hrm_timelogs where project_id matches. Aggregation: membersCount = COUNT(*) from erp_hrm_project_members where project_id matches.

totalActiveEmployees.description: Count of all employees with active status within the organization, excluding soft-deleted records.
totalActiveEmployees.x-autobe-specification: Computed as COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_employees WHERE organization_id = current_org_context AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL. This counts all employees with active status in the current organization, excluding soft-deleted records.

weeklyHours.description: Total hours logged by all employees in the current week (Monday through Sunday), calculated from timelog durations converted to decimal hours.
weeklyHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed as COALESCE(SUM(duration), 0) / 60 FROM erp_hrm_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_employees, filtered by organization_id and date range from Monday 00:00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59 of the current week. Duration is stored in minutes, converted to decimal hours by dividing by 60.

pendingApprovals.description: Count of timesheets with 'submitted' status awaiting manager review and approval.
pendingApprovals.x-autobe-specification: Computed as COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_timesheets joined with erp_hrm_employees, filtered by organization_id, status = 'submitted', and deleted_at IS NULL. This represents timesheets that have been submitted by employees and are awaiting manager review.

budgetAlerts.description: List of active projects where logged hours exceed 80% of allocated budget hours, requiring attention to prevent budget overrun.
budgetAlerts.x-autobe-specification: Computed by querying erp_hrm_projects with budget_hours IS NOT NULL, calculating actual_hours from erp_hrm_timelogs (SUM of durations / 60), computing utilization_percentage = (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100, and filtering projects where utilization > 80. Returns array of IErpHrmOrganizationDashboard.IBudgetAlert sorted by utilization_percentage DESC.

topPerformers.description: Top 5 employees ranked by total hours logged in the current week, providing visibility into team productivity.
topPerformers.x-autobe-specification: Computed by querying erp_hrm_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_employees for the current week (Monday to Sunday), filtering by organization_id and employee status = 'active', grouping by employee_id, summing duration, ordering by total_minutes DESC, and limiting to 5 results. Returns array of IErpHrmOrganizationDashboard.ITopPerformer with employee summary and hours_logged.

IErpHrmDashboard.IOrganization.description: Organization-level dashboard metrics visible to users with report viewing permission. Provides a comprehensive overview of organizational health including workforce size, time tracking activity, approval workload, budget utilization alerts, and performance rankings. All metrics are scoped to the current organization context and represent real-time aggregated data.
IErpHrmDashboard.IOrganization.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregated organization metrics computed from multiple tables in a single read-only query set:

1. totalActiveEmployees: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_employees WHERE organization_id = current_org AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL

2. weeklyHours: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(duration), 0) / 60 FROM erp_hrm_timelogs tl JOIN erp_hrm_employees e ON tl.employee_id = e.id WHERE e.organization_id = current_org AND tl.start_at >= :week_start AND tl.start_at < :week_end. Week boundaries: Monday 00:00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59 of current week.

3. pendingApprovals: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_timesheets ts JOIN erp_hrm_employees e ON ts.employee_id = e.id WHERE e.organization_id = current_org AND ts.status = 'submitted' AND ts.deleted_at IS NULL

4. budgetAlerts: For each erp_hrm_projects WHERE organization_id = current_org AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL: Calculate actual_hours from timelogs (SUM of durations / 60), compute utilization = actual_hours / budget_hours, filter where utilization > 0.8. Return as IErpHrmOrganizationDashboard.IBudgetAlert array sorted by utilization DESC.

5. topPerformers: SELECT employee_id, SUM(duration) as total_minutes FROM erp_hrm_timelogs tl JOIN erp_hrm_employees e ON tl.employee_id = e.id WHERE e.organization_id = current_org AND e.status = 'active' AND tl.start_at >= :week_start AND tl.start_at < :week_end GROUP BY employee_id ORDER BY total_minutes DESC LIMIT 5. Return as IErpHrmOrganizationDashboard.ITopPerformer array.

All queries scoped to organization_id from authenticated session context. Only computed for users with 'report:view' permission. Consider caching results for 5-10 minutes to reduce database load.

scenario.draft:
Test the complete successful registration flow for a new guest user.

**Test Flow:**
1. Send POST request to /erpHrm/auth/guest/join with valid registration data including:
   - Unique email address
   - Valid password meeting security requirements (8+ characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, special character)
   - Display name for the user profile
   - Complete organization configuration (name, currency, timezone, fiscal start month)
   - Session tracking information (href, referrer)

2. Verify response contains IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized with:
   - Unique member ID (UUID)
   - Valid JWT access token
   - Valid refresh token
   - Token expiration timestamps (access token ~15 minutes, refresh token ~7 days)
   - Session information

3. Validate business outcomes:
   - Member record created with correct email and display name
   - Organization created with provided configuration
   - Member assigned as owner of the created organization
   - User can authenticate subsequent API calls using the returned access token

**Validation Points:**
- Response status is 201 Created
- All required response fields are present and valid
- Access token can be used in Authorization header for member-scoped operations
- Organization exists with correct owner assignment

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /erpHrm/auth/guest/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'guest' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_success

scenario.draft:
Test that registration is rejected when attempting to register with an email address that already exists in the system.

**Test Flow:**
1. First, complete a successful registration with email 'existing@example.com' to establish a registered member
2. Attempt a second registration with the same email address 'existing@example.com' but different display name, password, and organization details

**Validation Points:**
- First registration succeeds with 201 Created
- Second registration is rejected with appropriate error status (409 Conflict)
- Error response indicates the email is already registered
- No duplicate member record is created
- Original member's data remains unchanged
- No second organization is created for the duplicate attempt

**Business Rule:**
Email addresses must be unique across all registered users. This is a platform-wide constraint to prevent duplicate accounts and ensure each member has a single identity across all organizations.

scenario.draft:
Test the successful token refresh flow with token rotation.

1. Use the refresh token from the prerequisite join operation to call the refresh endpoint
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 with valid IErpHrmGuest.IAuthorized structure
3. Validate that the response contains:
   - A new access token (different from any previous access token)
   - A new refresh token (different from the one used in the request)
   - Access token expiration timestamp (expired_at) set to approximately 15 minutes in the future
   - Refresh token deadline (refreshable_until) set to 7 days in the future
4. Verify that the old refresh token used in the request is now invalidated and cannot be used again
5. Attempt to use the new access token to verify it is valid and accepted by authenticated endpoints
6. Verify the new refresh token can be used for subsequent refresh operations

This test validates the core token refresh functionality and the security measure of token rotation, where each refresh operation issues a completely new token pair and invalidates the old refresh token to prevent token reuse attacks.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member account and obtain the initial refresh token that will be used to test the refresh operation. This establishes the authenticated session context.

functions.name: test_api_guest_refresh_token_rotation

scenario.draft:
Test the security mechanism that detects refresh token reuse and revokes all session tokens.

1. Use the refresh token from the prerequisite join operation to perform a successful refresh
2. Store the original refresh token (now invalidated) and the new refresh token received from step 1
3. Attempt to use the invalidated original refresh token again to call the refresh endpoint
4. Verify the response returns HTTP 403 Forbidden, indicating token revocation due to detected token reuse
5. Verify that attempting to use the new refresh token (from step 1) also fails with 401 or 403, confirming all tokens for that session have been revoked
6. Verify the member must re-authenticate by joining or logging in again to obtain new valid tokens

This test validates a critical security feature: when a previously-used refresh token is presented, the system detects potential token theft and revokes all tokens for that session to protect the member's account. Test Steps:

2. Call the list project members endpoint with a search term matching part of an employee's display name
3. Verify only members with matching display names are returned
4. Verify the search performs partial matching (e.g., searching 'John' matches 'John Smith', 'Johnny Doe')
5. Verify case-insensitive matching (e.g., searching 'john' matches 'John Smith')

Technical Details:

Prerequisites:
1. Create a member account via join endpoint
2. Organization setup creates various activity log entries with different action types

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as a member with org:manage permission
2. Call the activity logs endpoint with action_type filter (e.g., 'employee_invited', 'project_created', 'timesheet_approved', 'role_assigned')
3. Verify the response contains only activity logs matching the specified action type
4. Verify each returned entry has actionType matching the filter value exactly
5. Verify pagination metadata accurately reflects the filtered result count
6. Test with multiple different action types to verify filter works for various values
7. Test case-insensitivity or exact match behavior as specified in the implementation

Expected Result: Returns only activity log entries where action_type matches the filter value, demonstrating the system's ability to segment audit trail data by action category for focused compliance review.

scenario.draft:
Test the behavior when filtering activity logs returns no matching results, ensuring proper handling of empty data scenarios.

Prerequisites:
1. Create a member account via join endpoint

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as a member with org:manage permission
2. Call the activity logs endpoint with filters that match no records:
   - Use a date range (from/to) that is outside the period when any activity occurred
   - OR use an action_type that hasn't occurred in the organization
   - OR use a member_id that hasn't performed any actions
3. Verify the response structure:
   - pagination object with current page = 1, records = 0, pages = 0
   - data array is empty ([])
4. Verify no error is thrown for empty results
5. Verify the response status is successful (200 OK)
6. Verify pagination metadata is accurate (not showing negative values or errors)

Expected Result: Returns a valid paginated response with empty data array and zero record count, demonstrating graceful handling of scenarios where no activity logs match the specified filters.

scenario.draft:
Test successful retrieval of an activity log entry by a member with org:manage permission within their organization context.

Setup: Member authenticates and joins an organization where they have org:manage permission (owner or manager role). The organization has at least one activity log entry from a previous organizational action (such as employee creation, project creation, or timesheet approval).

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as a member with org:manage permission in the organization
2. Retrieve an activity log entry by its UUID
3. Verify the response contains complete activity log information including:
   - Unique identifier (id) matching the requested UUID
   - Action type (e.g., 'employee_invited', 'project_created', 'timesheet_approved')
   - Entity type and entity_id referencing the affected resource
   - Member details of who performed the action
   - Organization context matching the current organization
   - Created timestamp indicating when the action occurred
   - Optional details field with contextual information
4. Verify the member relation includes performer identification (id, email, displayName)
5. Verify the organization relation matches the current organization context

Validation: The activity log entry is successfully retrieved with all required fields populated, demonstrating proper audit trail access for compliance and oversight purposes. The member performing the action is correctly identified, and the organizational context is properly maintained.

scenario.draft:
Test that a member cannot retrieve activity log entries from a different organization, validating multi-tenant data isolation.

Setup: Two separate organizations exist, each with their own activity log entries. Member A belongs to Organization A with org:manage permission. Organization B has activity log entries from its own operations.

Test Steps:
1. Authenticate as Member A and establish organization context in Organization A
2. Obtain an activity log ID from Organization B (from a different member's actions)
3. Attempt to retrieve that activity log entry using the GET endpoint
4. Verify the system returns 404 Not Found (not 403, to avoid information disclosure about existence)

Validation: Cross-organization access is properly blocked, ensuring multi-tenant data isolation. The activity log query includes an organization_id filter that prevents access to logs outside the current organization context. This protects the confidentiality of audit trail information across organizational boundaries.

Security Consideration: The system should return 404 rather than 403 to avoid confirming the existence of activity logs in other organizations, preventing information leakage about other tenants' activities.

- Projects with budget_hours = 0 should be excluded to prevent division by zero

- Confirm budget_alerts are sorted by utilization_percentage in descending order

scenario.draft:
Test successful submission of a draft timesheet containing timelogs.

Setup steps:
1. Authenticate as a member via join endpoint
2. Create an organization (member becomes owner)
3. Create an employee record for the authenticated member
4. Create a project for timelogs
5. Create at least one timelog entry for the employee within a specific week

- Verify the returned timesheet has status changed from 'draft' to 'submitted'
- Verify submitted_at timestamp is populated with current time
- Verify the timesheet retains all associated timelogs

scenario.draft:
Test that submitting a timesheet for a week is blocked when another timesheet for that same week is already in 'submitted' or 'approved' status.

This test requires executing the submit operation twice - first to submit one timesheet successfully, then to verify the second submission is blocked. The test harness must handle this two-phase execution.

Setup steps (prerequisites):
1. Authenticate as a member via join endpoint
2. Create an organization
3. Create an employee record
4. Create a project
5. Create timelogs for the employee within a specific target week
6. Create first draft timesheet (Timesheet A) for that week
7. Create second draft timesheet (Timesheet B) for the SAME week (same week_start_date, different timesheet ID)

Test execution (two-phase):
Phase 1 - First submission:
- Call POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}/submit with Timesheet A ID
- Verify successful submission (status changes to 'submitted')
- Record the submitted_at timestamp

Phase 2 - Duplicate week submission attempt:
- Call POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets/{timesheetId}/submit with Timesheet B ID
- Verify the response returns 400 Bad Request status
- Verify the error message indicates another timesheet for this week is already submitted or approved
- Verify Timesheet B status remains 'draft'
- Verify Timesheet A is unaffected (still 'submitted')

Business validation:
- Confirm the system enforces the one-timesheet-per-week-per-employee rule for submitted/approved status
- Multiple drafts can coexist for the same week, but only one can progress to submitted/approved
- This prevents duplicate work records and payroll conflicts
- The first submitted timesheet blocks subsequent submissions until it is rejected

plan.thinking: Collectable Create DTO for custom roles. Maps directly to erp_hrm_roles table. The 'name' field maps to erp_hrm_roles.name, and 'permissions' array creates records in erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table. The organization_id FK is derived from the authenticated member's current organization context, not from the request body, requiring references from auth context.

IErpHrmOrganization.ICreate is a Create DTO for creating new organizations. It maps to the erp_hrm_organizations database table. The owner_id foreign key is not included in the request body - it comes from the authenticated member who creates the organization. This requires references to both the member (authorized actor) and the session (authorized session).

Collects IErpHrmEmployee.ICreate to erp_hrm_employees table. The Create DTO contains email (for member resolution via lookup), roleId (FK to role), departmentId (optional FK), position, and employmentType. The organization_id foreign key is not included in the DTO body - it must be sourced from the authorized session context where the current organization is stored. Member is resolved from email lookup, not from auth context, so only organization reference is needed.

IErpHrmTimelog.ICreate is a Create DTO for creating time entries. It maps to erp_hrm_timelogs database table as confirmed by x-autobe-database-schema annotation. The employee_id foreign key is derived from the authenticated session (authorized actor), not provided in the request body. Project_id and task_id are included in the DTO body and are not external references.

Collectable Create DTO for task creation. Maps to erp_hrm_tasks table. The project_id foreign key is provided via path parameter projectId, not in the request body. employee_id and parent_task_id are in the DTO body as optional fields, so they don't need external references.

Create DTO for department creation operation. Maps to erp_hrm_departments table. The organization_id foreign key is not provided in the request body but is extracted from the authenticated member's current organization context via JWT session, requiring a reference from authorized session.

Create DTO for timesheet creation mapping to erp_hrm_timesheets table. The week_start_date is provided in request body, but employee_id is derived from authenticated member's employee record. Therefore collector needs reference to employee entity from authorized actor.

Collectable Create DTO for project member assignment. Maps to erp_hrm_project_members table with employee_id and role fields. The project FK (erp_hrm_project_id) comes from path parameter projectId, requiring external reference.

IErpHrmTimer.ICreate is a Create DTO for starting a new timer session. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation maps it to erp_hrm_timers table. The DTO provides project_id (required FK to project) and task_id (optional FK to task) in the request body. However, erp_hrm_employee_id is NOT in the DTO - it's derived from the authenticated employee context via JWT token as stated in the specification. Therefore, erp_hrm_employees is an external reference from the authorized actor.

Create DTO for projects, maps to erp_hrm_projects table. The organization_id foreign key is not included in the request body - it is populated from the authenticated member's current organization context.

Collectable Create DTO for employment contracts. Maps to erp_hrm_contracts table. The erp_hrm_employee_id foreign key is provided via path parameter employeeId, requiring a reference to erp_hrm_employees.

Collectable Create DTO for invitation creation. Maps to erp_hrm_invitations table. The organization_id foreign key is sourced from the path parameter organizationId (not in request body), requiring a reference. The role_id is provided directly in the request body via roleId field.
Lightweight department summary for list displays. Maps to erp_hrm_departments table with LEFT JOIN to parent department. Read DTO (ISummary), DB-backed, direct mapping to primary table.

Lightweight organization summary DTO maps directly to erp_hrm_organizations table. Contains direct field mappings (id, name, description, logoImage, currency, timezone, fiscalStartMonth, createdAt) plus computed fields (isOwner, role) and nested owner relation from erp_hrm_members. Transformable as it's a Read DTO with DB-backed data.

Transformable DTO: IErpHrmGuest.ISummary is a lightweight summary for list displays. Maps to erp_hrm_guests table with direct property mapping (id, fingerprint, created_at) and computed sessions_count field aggregated from erp_hrm_guest_sessions. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms erp_hrm_guests as the primary table.

Transformable DTO mapping to erp_hrm_organizations table. Complete organization entity with nested owner field (IErpHrmMember.ISummary) requiring JOIN with erp_hrm_members. Used for API responses with direct DB-backed data.

Transforms erp_hrm_guest_sessions to IErpHrmGuestSession.ISummary with nested guest relation and computed duration field (expired_at - created_at). Direct mapping for id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at with JOIN to erp_hrm_guests for guest fingerprint.

IErpHrmMember is a Read DTO for API responses containing member profile data. It maps directly to erp_hrm_members table with properties id, email, display_name, avatar_image, phone_number, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms the table mapping.

Transformable Read DTO mapping to erp_hrm_guest_sessions database table. Contains direct column mappings for session tracking data (id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at) and nested guest relation via foreign key. The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms the table mapping.

Transformable DTO - summary type for member profiles used in list displays. Maps directly to erp_hrm_members database table as indicated by x-autobe-database-schema annotation. Contains essential member fields (id, email, displayName, avatarImage, phoneNumber, createdAt, deletedAt) with direct property mappings to database columns.

IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary is a lightweight employee summary DTO for list displays. It maps directly to erp_hrm_employees table with JOINs to erp_hrm_members (for member profile), erp_hrm_roles (for role assignment), and erp_hrm_departments (for optional department affiliation). The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms 'erp_hrm_employees' as the primary table. This is a transformable Read DTO that requires a transformer to convert database records with nested relations into the summary format.

IErpHrmEmployee is a complete employee entity used for API responses. It has x-autobe-database-schema='erp_hrm_employees' indicating direct mapping to the erp_hrm_employees table. The DTO contains direct properties (id, position, employment_type, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and nested relations (member, organization, role, department). Transformable read DTO for session management. Maps to erp_hrm_member_sessions table with direct column mappings (id, ip, href, referrer, timestamps) and JOIN relations to member (erp_hrm_members) and organization (erp_hrm_organizations) for nested summary objects.

Transformable read DTO mapping to erp_hrm_roles table. Contains direct column mappings, organization relation fetched via FK join, and computed permissions array from erp_hrm_role_permissions junction table.

Transforms erp_hrm_guests to IErpHrmGuest with nested sessions relation from erp_hrm_guest_sessions. This is a Read DTO mapping directly to database table erp_hrm_guests with properties id, fingerprint, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, and computed sessions array via has-many relation.

Complete employment contract entity that transforms erp_hrm_contracts table with employee relation join. Contains direct column mappings (id, start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) plus employee relation via IErpHrmEmployee.ISummary. Read DTO for API responses - transformable.

It contains direct column mappings (id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, updated_at, expired_at) and JOIN relations for member (IErpHrmMember.ISummary) and organization (IErpHrmOrganization.ISummary, nullable). IErpHrmActivityLog maps directly to erp_hrm_activity_logs table. It has x-autobe-database-schema annotation indicating the mapped table. Transformable DTO with x-autobe-database-schema annotation pointing to erp_hrm_timesheets. Read DTO for API responses with direct database mapping.   /**

Each contract belongs to exactly one employee and tracks the employee's pay rate, payment frequency, and expected working hours.
   *
   * When a new contract is created for an employee who already has an active contract, the system automatically ends the previous contract by setting its end date to the day before the new contract's start date. This ensures that only one contract can be active at any given time per employee, maintaining a clean employment history chain.
   *
   * Security considerations: Only users with the employee:manage permission can create contracts. The employee must exist within the current organization context. The operation validates all required fields including start date, pay rate, pay period, and working hours per week.

   * 4. Check if the employee has an existing active contract (start_date <= now AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date > now)):
   *    - If yes, update the previous active contract's end_date to (new contract's start_date - 1 day)
   * 5. Create the new contract record with:
   *    - erp_hrm_employee_id = employeeId from path
   *    - start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes from request body
   *    - created_at, updated_at = current timestamp
   *    - deleted_at = null
   * 6. Return the created contract with all fields including the generated id.
   *
   * Authorization: Requires employee:manage permission within the organization.
   *
   * Error handling:
   * - 403 if user lacks employee:manage permission
   * - 404 if employee not found in organization
   * - 400 if validation fails for required fields
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async create(
    @MemberAuth()
    member: MemberPayload,

  /**
   * Retrieve a paginated list of employment contracts for a specific employee within the organization.

The response includes all contracts maintained as historical records throughout the employee's tenure, sorted with the most recent contracts appearing first.
   *
   * Each contract in the list includes essential employment terms: start date, end date (null for ongoing contracts), pay rate, pay period, and working hours per week. The list supports filtering by date ranges to view contracts from specific periods, and can filter between active and historical contracts.
   *
   * Contract status identification:
   * - An active contract has a start date that has passed and either no end date (ongoing) or an end date in the future
   * - A historical contract has an end date in the past and is immutable for compliance purposes
   *
   * Authorization:

    }

  /**
   * Retrieve detailed information about a specific employment contract.
   *
   * This operation returns complete contract details for a given employee, including the employment terms such as compensation (pay_rate), payment frequency (pay_period), expected weekly commitment (working_hours_per_week), and validity period (start_date and end_date).
   *
   * Access control is enforced based on the viewer's relationship to the employee:
   * - Employees can always view their own contracts
   * - Users with 'employee:view' permission can view any employee's contracts within the organization
   * - Users cannot access contracts from other organizations
   *
   * The response indicates whether the contract is currently active based on the start and end dates. An active contract has a start date that has passed and either no end date (ongoing) or an end date in the future.
   *
   * This endpoint is typically used after listing contracts to view complete details of a specific contract record, or when reviewing employment terms for payroll and HR purposes.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param employeeId The unique identifier of the employee whose contract is being retrieved (UUID format, scoped to current organization)
   * @param contractId The unique identifier of the contract to retrieve (UUID format, must belong to the specified employee)

   *
   * Implementation steps:

   *    - If viewing own contracts: the user's member.id must match the employee's erp_hrm_member_id

   * 3. Query erp_hrm_contracts table for the contract matching both employeeId and contractId
   * 4. Filter out soft-deleted contracts (deleted_at is null)
   * 5. Return the contract with all fields: id, start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, notes, created_at, updated_at
   * 6. Include a computed 'is_active' boolean field: true if start_date <= now AND (end_date is null OR end_date > now)

The contract must be currently active—meaning its start date has passed and its end date is either null (ongoing) or in the future. Past contracts with end dates in the past are immutable historical records that cannot be modified.
   *
   * ## Editable Fields
   *
   * The following contract fields can be modified:
   * - **end_date**: The termination date of the contract. Setting this to a past date immediately locks the contract as a historical record.
   * - **pay_rate**: The compensation amount, interpreted according to the pay period.
   * - **pay_period**: The payment frequency—hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.
   * - **working_hours_per_week**: The expected weekly commitment in hours.
   * - **notes**: Additional context or special terms for the contract.
   *
   * ## Immutable Fields
   *
   * The **start_date** field cannot be changed once a contract is created. This ensures the integrity of the employment timeline.
   *
   * ## Permission Requirements
   *
   * Only users with the `employee:manage` permission can update contracts. Employees cannot modify their own contracts, even though they can view them. This separation ensures proper authorization control over employment terms.
   *
   * ## Related Operations
   *
   * - `GET /employees/{employeeId}/contracts` — View all contracts for an employee
   * - `POST /employees/{employeeId}/contracts` — Create a new contract (automatically ends previous active contract)
   * - `GET /employees/{employeeId}/contracts/{contractId}` — View a specific contract
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param employeeId The UUID of the employee whose contract is being updated. The employee must belong to the current organization context.
   * @param contractId The UUID of the contract to update. The contract must belong to the specified employee and must be active (start_date passed, end_date null or future).
   * @param body Contract update details. Only active contracts can be modified. The start_date field is immutable and cannot be changed.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor member
   * @x-autobe-specification Update an existing employment contract for an employee.
   *
   * ## Validation Steps
   * 1. Verify user has employee:manage permission in the organization
   * 2. Verify the employee exists and belongs to the current organization context

   * 4. Verify the contract is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
   * 5. Verify the contract is active (editable):
   *    - Contract is active if: start_date <= now AND (end_date is null OR end_date > now)
   *    - If contract end_date is in the past, reject with error: contract is historical and immutable
   * 6. Validate request body fields:
   *    - pay_rate: required, must be positive number
   *    - pay_period: required, must be one of 'hourly', 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly'
   *    - working_hours_per_week: required, must be positive integer (typically 1-60)
   *    - end_date: optional, if provided must be >= start_date and cannot be in the past
   *    - notes: optional, free text
   *
   * ## Business Rules
   * - start_date cannot be modified (not included in IUpdate schema)
   * - If end_date is set to a date in the past, the contract immediately becomes a past contract and locked
   * - Only one contract per employee can be active at any time
   * - Users without employee:manage permission receive 403 Forbidden
   * - Employees cannot edit their own contracts even if they have view permission
   *
   * ## Database Operations
   * 1. Begin transaction
   * 2. Update erp_hrm_contracts record with new values
   * 3. Set updated_at to current timestamp
   * 4. Commit transaction
   * 5. Return updated contract with employee relation loaded
   *
   * ## Error Responses
   * - 403: User lacks employee:manage permission
   * - 403: Employee attempting to edit own contract
   * - 404: Employee not found or not in organization

   * - 409: Contract is historical (end_date in past), cannot be edited

import { TypedBody, TypedParam, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { IErpHrmTimesheet } from "../../../../../api/structures/IErpHrmTimesheet";
import { MemberAuth } from "../../../../../decorators/MemberAuth";
import { MemberPayload } from "../../../../../decorators/payload/MemberPayload";
import { deleteErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogsTimelogId } from "../../../../../providers/deleteErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogsTimelogId";
import { patchErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogs } from "../../../../../providers/patchErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogs";
import { postErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogs } from "../../../../../providers/postErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogs";

@Controller("/erpHrm/member/timesheets/:timesheetId/timelogs")
export class ErphrmMemberTimesheetsTimelogsController {
  /**
   * Add existing timelogs to a draft timesheet for the current employee.
   *
   * This operation allows employees to manually add timelogs to their draft timesheet that were not automatically included during timesheet creation. The timelogs must belong to the same employee as the timesheet and must fall within the week date range defined by the timesheet's week_start_date and week_end_date.
   *
   * The operation is only permitted when the timesheet has 'draft' status. Draft timesheets can be freely modified by the employee before submission. Once a timesheet is submitted, approved, or rejected, this operation is no longer available for that timesheet.
   *
   * After adding timelogs, the timesheet's total_hours is automatically recalculated by summing the duration of all included timelogs divided by 60. The operation returns the updated timesheet with the new total hours reflected.
   *
   * Related to the erp_hrm_timesheets table (timesheet aggregation) and erp_hrm_timelogs table (individual time entries). The association is stored in the erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param timesheetId UUID of the draft timesheet to add timelogs to
   * @param body Array of timelog IDs to add to the draft timesheet
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor member
   * @x-autobe-specification Add existing timelogs to a draft timesheet.
   *
   * Implementation steps:
   * 1. Fetch the timesheet by timesheetId from erp_hrm_timesheets table
   * 2. Verify the timesheet exists and belongs to the current employee (from session context)
   * 3. Verify the timesheet status is 'draft' - reject with 403 if not draft
   * 4. For each timelogId in the request body:
   *    a. Fetch the timelog from erp_hrm_timelogs table
   *    b. Verify the timelog belongs to the same employee as the timesheet
   *    c. Verify the timelog date falls within the timesheet's week_start_date and week_end_date
   *    d. Verify the timelog is not already included in another submitted/approved timesheet
   *    e. Create a new record in erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table
   * 5. Recalculate total_hours by summing all linked timelogs' duration_minutes / 60
   * 6. Update the timesheet's updated_at timestamp
   * 7. Return the updated timesheet with recalculated total_hours
   *
   * Error conditions:
   * - 404: Timesheet not found
   * - 403: Timesheet does not belong to current employee
   * - 403: Timesheet is not in draft status (submitted/approved/rejected)
   * - 400: Timelog does not belong to the same employee
   * - 400: Timelog date is outside the timesheet week range
   * - 400: Timelog is already included in another submitted/approved timesheet
   * - 400: Timelog already exists in this timesheet
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Post()
  public async addTimelogs(
    @MemberAuth()
    member: MemberPayload,
    @TypedParam("timesheetId")
    timesheetId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IErpHrmTimesheet.IAddTimelog,
  ): Promise<IErpHrmTimesheet> {
    try {
      return await postErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogs({
        member,
        timesheetId,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Modify the timelog associations of a draft timesheet by adding or removing individual time entries.
   *
   * This operation enables employees to manage the contents of their draft timesheets by explicitly specifying which timelogs to add or remove. Draft timesheets start with all timelogs for the week automatically included, but employees may need to adjust the contents before submission.
   *
   * **Authorization Requirements:**
   * - The employee who owns the timesheet can modify their own draft timesheets
   * - Users with 'time:manage' permission can modify any timesheet, including submitted and approved timesheets (time management permission override)
   * - Deactivated employees cannot modify timesheets
   *
   * **Status-Based Restrictions:**
   * - Draft timesheets: Can be modified by the owning employee
   * - Submitted timesheets: Cannot be modified unless the user has 'time:manage' permission; must be rejected first to return to draft status
   * - Approved timesheets: Cannot be modified unless the user has 'time:manage' permission; all included timelogs are locked
   * - Rejected timesheets: Can be modified (treated as draft for modification purposes)
   *
   * **Business Rules:**
   * - Timelogs being added must belong to the same employee who owns the timesheet
   * - Timelogs being added must fall within the timesheet's week date range (between week_start_date and week_end_date)
   * - Timelogs cannot be included in multiple timesheets for the same week
   * - When timelogs are added or removed, the total_hours is recalculated automatically
   *
   * **Related Operations:**
   * - GET /timesheets/{timesheetId} — View the timesheet details including associated timelogs
   * - PATCH /timesheets/{timesheetId}/submit — Submit the timesheet for approval
   * - PATCH /timesheets/{timesheetId}/approve — Approve a submitted timesheet
   * - PATCH /timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject — Reject a submitted timesheet with a reason
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param timesheetId Unique identifier of the timesheet whose timelog associations are being modified
   * @param body Arrays of timelog IDs to add to and remove from the timesheet
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor member
   * @x-autobe-specification Implementation steps:
   *
   * 1. **Authentication & Authorization Check**
   *    - Verify the authenticated user is a member with an active employee record in the organization
   *    - Fetch the timesheet by timesheetId
   *    - Verify the timesheet belongs to the organization context
   *    - Check if the user is the owner of the timesheet (employee_id matches) OR has 'time:manage' permission
   *    - If neither, return 403 Forbidden
   *
   * 2. **Employee Status Check**
   *    - Query erp_hrm_employees to verify the employee is not deactivated (status = 'active')
   *    - If deactivated, return 403 Forbidden
   *
   * 3. **Timesheet Status Validation**
   *    - If timesheet.status is 'submitted' or 'approved' and user does NOT have 'time:manage' permission:
   *      - Return 400 Bad Request with message indicating the timesheet cannot be modified in current status
   *    - Draft and rejected timesheets can be modified
   *
   * 4. **Timelog Validation (for 'add' array)**
   *    - For each timelogId in the 'add' array:
   *      - Query erp_hrm_timelogs to verify the timelog exists
   *      - Verify timelog.employee_id matches timesheet.employee_id (same employee)
   *      - Verify timelog.date is within [week_start_date, week_end_date] range
   *      - Query erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs to verify this timelog is not already included in another timesheet for the same week
   *      - If any validation fails, return 400 Bad Request with specific error
   *
   * 5. **Timelog Validation (for 'remove' array)**
   *    - For each timelogId in the 'remove' array:
   *      - Query erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs to verify the timelog is currently associated with this timesheet
   *      - If not associated, skip or return error based on idempotency preference
   *
   * 6. **Database Transaction**
   *    - Begin transaction
   *    - Delete from erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs where timesheet_id = timesheetId AND timelog_id IN (remove array)
   *    - Insert into erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs for each timelog in add array
   *    - Recalculate total_hours: SUM(timelogs.duration) / 60 from all associated timelogs
   *    - Update erp_hrm_timesheets set total_hours = calculated value, updated_at = now()
   *    - Commit transaction
   *
   * 7. **Response Construction**
   *    - Fetch updated timesheet with associations
   *    - Return IErpHrmTimesheet with updated total_hours
   *
   * **Error Handling:**
   * - 404 Not Found: Timesheet or timelog does not exist
   * - 403 Forbidden: User not authorized to modify this timesheet or employee deactivated
   * - 400 Bad Request: Timesheet status doesn't allow modification, timelog doesn't belong to employee, timelog outside week range, timelog already in another timesheet
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async updateTimelogs(
    @MemberAuth()
    member: MemberPayload,
    @TypedParam("timesheetId")
    timesheetId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IErpHrmTimesheet.IUpdateTimelog,
  ): Promise<IErpHrmTimesheet> {
    try {
      return await patchErpHrmMemberTimesheetsTimesheetIdTimelogs({
        member,
        timesheetId,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Remove a timelog entry from a timesheet's timelog collection.
   *
   * This operation allows employees to manage which time entries are included in their timesheet before submission. The timelog is disassociated from the timesheet but the underlying time record is preserved, allowing it to be added to a different timesheet or remain as an unsubmitted entry.
   *
   * **Authorization Rules:**
   *
   * Employees can only remove timelogs from their own timesheets that are in 'draft' or 'rejected' status. Once a timesheet is submitted (status 'submitted'), the employee cannot modify its contents until it is either approved (locked permanently) or rejected (returns to draft status).
   *
   * Users with the 'time:manage' permission can remove timelogs from any timesheet regardless of status, providing an administrative override for special circumstances.
   *
   * **Related Operations:**
   *
   * - POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/timelogs — Add a timelog to a timesheet
   * - GET /timesheets/{timesheetId} — View timesheet details with all included timelogs
   * - GET /timelogs/{timelogId} — View individual timelog details
   *
   * **Post-Operation Effects:**
   *
   * After successful removal, the timesheet's total hours are automatically recalculated based on the remaining timelogs. The timesheet's updated_at timestamp is refreshed to reflect this change.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param timesheetId Unique identifier of the timesheet from which to remove the timelog. The timesheet must exist and belong to the current organization.
   * @param timelogId Unique identifier of the timelog to remove from the timesheet. Must be currently associated with the specified timesheet.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor member
   * @x-autobe-specification Delete the junction record from erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs table where timesheet_id matches the path parameter and timelog_id matches the path parameter. Before deletion:
   *
   * 1. Validate the timesheet exists and belongs to the current organization context
   * 2. Validate the timelog exists and belongs to the same employee as the timesheet
   * 3. Check authorization:
   *    - If user is the employee who owns the timesheet: timesheet.status must be 'draft' or 'rejected'
   *    - If user has 'time:manage' permission: no status restriction
   * 4. Return 403 Forbidden if authorization check fails
   * 5. Return 404 Not Found if the timesheet-timelog association doesn't exist
   *
   * After deletion:
   * 1. Recalculate timesheet.total_hours by summing duration/60 of all remaining associated timelogs
   * 2. Update timesheet.updated_at timestamp
